title: STP-001 · Venue Analysis
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-01 · drill · Venue Analysis Map Drill
  • MIS-WB-001 · mission · Read Today's Spot
  • MIS-WB-001-A · mission · Group Venue Read (coach)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-01] You drew the spot (sand or paper) with the five zones marked: safe zone, impact zone, entry, exit, and where you will surf.
  2. [DRL-WB-01] You can describe the day's conditions and point out the main hazards and currents on your map.
  3. [DRL-WB-01] You state whether conditions match your level today, with a simple session plan.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-001] You describe today's conditions and point to the safe zone.
  2. [MIS-WB-001] You point out the impact zone and name the main hazards and currents.
  3. [MIS-WB-001] You say your entry and exit, whether the day fits your level, and a simple session plan.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-001 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Coach cues + Mastery criteria); lessons STP-001 tiene el mismo texto sin la tabla del coach)

**Biomechanics** — No specific biomechanics — this is observational. Your body stands still on the beach. Your eyes work: scanning, identifying, comparing. **Common errors** — Rushing the analysis; vague reading of the spot; not waiting long enough to see big sets; failing to identify outside reference points; poor current identification; no clear entry/exit plan; not matching conditions to your level. **Coach cue** — Show me WHERE. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You describe the day's general conditions and identify the safe zone with precision. 2. You recognize the impact zone and point out the main hazards and currents. 3. You explain your entry/exit points and state whether conditions match your level, with a simple session plan.

La lección tiene un problema (1):

  • Boilerplate de las 9 lecciones STP-001..009: "When you can confirm all the self-checks consistently across 3 different sessions, you are ready for the next step. Your coach confirms mastery in the water." — conteo (3 sesiones) + coletilla del coach. Si se queda, que sea regla de graduación, no criterio del paso.

Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. You point to one land reference and one outside reference.
  2. You point to the safe zone and the impact zone.
  3. You point to where the current runs and name today's hazards.
  4. You point to your entry and your exit, then call it: go or no-go for your level.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Before you walk in, read the real spot from the beach — point and say it: one land reference and one outside reference, the safe zone and the impact zone, where the current runs and today's hazards, your entry and your exit. Then call it: go or no-go for your level, and one goal for the session.

  1. [DRL-WB-002-A] All joints moved
  2. [DRL-WB-002-A] Visible cobra simulation
  3. [DRL-WB-002-A] Breath connection at end

**Biomechanics** — Emphasis on mobility and activation of shoulders, scapulae, trunk, hips, ankles, core, obliques, posture, and knee flexion patterns used in paddling, pop-up, posture, impact absorption, and basic rotation. **Common errors** — Skipping the warm-up entirely; doing a generic gym warm-up that has nothing to do with surfing; rushing through it; entering the water cold and stiff; skipping the breath / focus segment. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You execute all 4 segments fluidly without prompting. 2. Your body feels active and warm — not stiff or asleep. 3. You enter mentally focused, not scattered.

  3. You rehearse today's steps on the sand, low and controlled — nothing generic.
  4. You close with slow nose breathing, eyes closed — and say your one intention out loud before you open them.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Before every session, run the whole flow on the sand: mobility, activation, a rehearsal of today's steps, breath. Walk to the water warm and with one intention.

title: STP-003 · Grab Board
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-003-A · drill · Grab Board: Lift and Carry
  • MIS-WB-003 · mission · Carry Board From Rack to Water Edge

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-003-A] Every lift: knees bent, back straight, both hands on the rails.
  2. [DRL-WB-003-A] Side or under-arm carry, hand on the rail, no swinging, never on your head.
  3. [DRL-WB-003-A] Set down gently, no slap, no scrape.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-003] Clean lift: both hands on the rails, knees bent, back straight.
  2. [MIS-WB-003] Controlled carry to the water edge — no dragging the fins, no swinging near other people.
  3. [MIS-WB-003] Board placed gently at the water edge.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-003 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Coach cues + Mastery criteria); lessons STP-003 idéntica sin tabla)

**Biomechanics** — Stand beside the center of the board. Keep the back straight. Bend the knees. Grip the rails with both hands. Lift with control and stabilize the board before moving. **Common errors** — Lifting with your back instead of your legs; holding the deck instead of the rails; swinging the board near other people; dragging the fins on the sand. **Coach cue** — Board at your side. Nose away. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You lift with proper mechanics every time (knees bent, back straight, both hands on rails). 2. You carry under control without swinging. 3. You set the board down gently — no slap.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (2):

  • Falta la regla de seguridad de la doctrina: nunca cargar la tabla sobre la cabeza (cuello); segunda carga = bajo la axila. Agregar a Common errors.
  • Fila de la tabla del coach "Drops board when whitewater hits | Firm grip, wide stance, lean into it" es de STP-006/007, no de Grab Board.
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. You stand beside the center of the board, knees bent, back straight.
  2. Both hands on the rails, never on the deck.
  3. The legs do the lift, back still straight — and the board is steady before your first step.
  4. Carry at your hip or under your arm, hand on the rail — never on your head, no swing, no fins dragging — and it goes down without a slap.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Take the board from the rack to the water's edge: stand beside the center, bend the knees, grab both rails and lift with your legs. Carry it at your hip or under your arm and set it down gently at the edge.

Drill

Sin cambios de estructura; sacar los conteos de Simulate y reps_recommended (el alumno pone la cantidad).
juego:
Juego

Sleeping Board

The board is asleep in your arms.

Rule: It makes a sound — slap, scrape, knock — it wakes up and you lost.

title: STP-004 · Walk Out
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-04 · drill · Walk Out Sand Entry Drill
  • MIS-WB-004 · mission · Walk Out to Waist-Deep Without Losing Control

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-04] You wait for a lull first.
  2. [DRL-WB-04] Feet drag the whole way; board at your side, body ocean-side.
  3. [DRL-WB-04] Waist depth, calm pace, board in hand.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-004] You arrive at waist-deep without losing the board, getting hit by foam, slipping on rocks, or panicking. Composure intact.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-004 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Coach cues + Mastery criteria); lessons STP-004 idéntica sin tabla)

**Biomechanics** — Walk with calm, stable steps. Drag the feet on sand. Keep the board at the side of the body. Stay oriented toward incoming whitewater. Maintain control and avoid rushing. **Common errors** — Walking with the board in front (gets pushed back into you); walking with the board behind (you can't see it); not waiting for a lull before entering; letting the board go sideways to a wave; rushing through unstable footing. **Coach cue** — Board to your SIDE. Always. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You enter the water without losing the board. 2. You arrive at waist-deep with composure. 3. You waited for a lull, not a set.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (2):

  • Biomechanics no dice hacia dónde apunta la nariz al entrar; agregar 'nose pointing into the incoming foam — against the direction the wave's energy travels'.
  • Fila del coach "Cannot control board through foam | Press tail to lift nose above foam line" pertenece a STP-006/007.
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. You watch the foam and step in on a lull, not on a set.
  2. Your feet slide along the bottom the whole way — no step lifts off the sand.
  3. Board at your side — never in front of you, never behind you, never between you and a foam.
  4. You face the incoming foam, nose into it, all the way to waist depth — walking pace, board still in your hands.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Walk in from the sand to waist depth on a lull: feet sliding on the bottom, board at your side — never in front of you, never behind you — you and the nose facing the incoming foam, at walking pace.

title: STP-005 · Put Board in the Water
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-005-A · drill · Waist-Deep Placement Drill
  • MIS-WB-005 · mission · Place Board for Sweet Spot Mounting

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-005-A] Board enters the water gently — no slap.
  2. [DRL-WB-005-A] Nose stays into the incoming waves — never parallel.
  3. [DRL-WB-005-A] 5-8 placements without losing the board.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-005] Gentle entry every time — no slap.
  2. [MIS-WB-005] Board floats with the nose into the waves, never sideways.
  3. [MIS-WB-005] 5-8 placements without losing the board — mission complete.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-005 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria) + lessons STP-005 (How you know you have it, ya corregida en nariz el 2026-09-02))

**Biomechanics** — Wait until the water reaches approximately waist height. Lower the board into the water with control. Do not rush or drop the board. **Common errors** — Slapping the board on the water; releasing too early; placing perpendicular to waves; not staying ready to grab if foam comes. **Mastery criteria** (MASTER-WB-06) — 1. Board enters the water gently — no slap. 2. Board stays parallel to waves. 3. 5–8 placements without losing the board. **lessons STP-005 (corregida)** — Board stays with the nose pointing into the incoming waves — never parallel.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (4):

  • MASTER-WB-06 § STP-005 Concept: "so it floats parallel to incoming waves" → debe decir "floats with the nose pointing into the incoming waves — against the direction the wave's energy travels" (como ya dice lessons STP-005).
  • Common errors: "placing perpendicular to waves" — está al revés; perpendicular a la línea de la ola ES lo correcto. Debe decir "placing sideways (parallel) to the wave line".
  • Mastery 2 (MASTER-WB-06): "Board stays parallel to waves" → "nose into the incoming waves — never sideways".
  • Mastery 3 (MASTER-WB-06 y lessons STP-005): "5–8 placements without losing the board" — conteo.
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. At waist depth you wait for the gap between foam lines before the board touches the water.
  2. Both hands on the rails, you lower it nose into the incoming waves, never sideways — no slap.
  3. You let go with open fingers — no push, no throw.
  4. Your hand stays at the rail, you on the ocean side — ready to grab it the moment foam moves it.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

At waist depth, in the gap between foam lines, lower the board onto the water with both hands on the rails — nose into the incoming waves, never sideways, no slap. Let go with open fingers, keep your hand at the rail and stay on the ocean side, ready to grab it.

title: STP-006 · Control Your Board
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-006-A · drill · Tail-Center Control Drill
  • MIS-WB-006 · mission · Manage Board Through Three Foam Lines → Manage the Board Through the Foam Lines (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-006-A] Nose stays pointed at the ocean — never sideways.
  2. [DRL-WB-006-A] Board never leaves your hands: tail and center.
  3. [DRL-WB-006-A] You stay on the ocean side of the board.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-006] Three foam lines in a row without losing the board.
  2. [MIS-WB-006] Board never sideways to the wave.
  3. [MIS-WB-006] Board never between you and the wave — mission complete.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-006 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria) + lessons STP-006 (How you know you have it, ya corregida en lado del cuerpo))

**Biomechanics** — One hand controls the tail and applies downward pressure for leverage. One hand stabilizes the center. The board stays at the side of the body and never directly in front. **Common errors** — Letting the board go sideways; standing in front of the board (foam pushes board into you); not maintaining hand grip; losing the board to foam. **Mastery criteria** (MASTER-WB-06) — 1. Board nose always pointed into foam — never sideways. 2. You pass 5–8 foam waves without losing board control. 3. Body stays between board and shore at all times. **lessons STP-006** — You stay on the ocean side of the board at all times.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (2):

  • MASTER-WB-06 § STP-006 Key concepts "Body between board and shore" y Mastery 3 "Body stays between board and shore at all times" → al revés; debe decir "You stay on the ocean side of the board — between the board and the wave" (como ya dice lessons STP-006).
  • Mastery 2 (MASTER-WB-06 y lessons STP-006): "You pass 5–8 foam waves without losing board control" — conteo.
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. One hand on the tail, one on the center — the board never leaves your hands.
  2. The board is beside you, nose into the foam, and you stay on its ocean side — never with the board between you and the wave.
  3. As the foam arrives, the tail hand pushes down so the nose rides up over it.
  4. If the board swings sideways, you pivot it from the tail back into the foam.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Stand waist-deep as the foam lines come, tail hand and center hand on the board, board beside you with the nose into the foam and you on the ocean side. Push the tail down as each foam reaches the nose so it rides over; if the board swings, pivot it from the tail back into the foam.

Drill

Measure: foam lines survived with the hand still on

title: STP-007 · Go Through Whitewater Standing
hoy:
HOY

  • MIS-WB-007-A · mission · Board Control Through Whitewater
  • DRL-WB-07 · drill · Whitewater Passage Drill
  • MIS-WB-007 · mission · Pass Through Five Foam Waves Standing → Pass Through Foam Waves Standing (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-07] Same hands every rep: tail and center.
  2. [DRL-WB-07] Tail pressure lifts the nose, arm extended, board straight.
  3. [DRL-WB-07] You step forward every rep, never back.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-007] 5 foam waves without losing balance.
  2. [MIS-WB-007] Board stays in your hands the whole way.
  3. [MIS-WB-007] After each wave you are further out, never pushed back.
  4. [MIS-WB-007-A cadena] Board never dropped, never between you and the foam.
  5. [MIS-WB-007-A cadena] Two-plus foam walls passed standing, moving forward.
  6. [MIS-WB-007-A cadena] You land composed.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-007 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Coach cues + Mastery criteria); lessons STP-007 idéntica sin tabla)

**Biomechanics** — Keep one hand on the tail and one near the center. Align the board straight toward the foam. Use tail pressure and an extended arm to lift the nose. For stronger foam, add knee flexion and a small jump for more power. **Common errors** — Stiff body — gets thrown back; standing tall — bad balance; releasing tail pressure too early; not progressing forward. **Coach cues** — Compact. Lean in. / Sink into your stance. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You pass 5 foam waves without losing balance. 2. Board stays connected to you throughout. 3. You progress forward (not backward) after each foam wave.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (1):

  • Mastery 1 (MASTER-WB-06 y lessons STP-007): "You pass 5 foam waves without losing balance" — conteo.
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Board straight at the foam, nose into it, before the foam arrives.
  2. Knees soft, body compact — you hold there until the foam reaches the nose.
  3. Tail pressed and held through the impact — other arm extended, you lean in — until the foam is past: no early release.
  4. You step forward as it passes under you; on stronger foam you bend the knees and add a small jump.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Waist-deep, board straight at the foam with the nose into it, one hand on the tail and one near the center. Compact, knees soft, wait for the foam to reach the nose; press the tail, extend the other arm and lean in — hold the press until the foam is past — then step forward. Stronger foam: bend the knees and add a small jump.

Drill

title: STP-008 · Turn Around Safely
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-008-A · drill · Safe Pivot Turn Drill
  • MIS-WB-008 · mission · Turn Around Safely 5 Times → Turn Around Safely (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. [DRL-WB-008-A] 5 turns, board controlled — never loose.
  2. [DRL-WB-008-A] Body on the ocean side — between the board and the wave — every turn.
  3. [DRL-WB-008-A] Each turn ends ready to paddle, not scrambling.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. [MIS-WB-008] 5 turns, board under control the whole time — never loose.
  2. [MIS-WB-008] Your body is between the board and the wave on every turn.
  3. [MIS-WB-008] You finish each turn ready to paddle, not scrambling.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-008 (Concept + Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria) + lessons STP-008 (How you know you have it, ya corregida))

**Concept** — Rotate the board 180 degrees while keeping your body between the board and the wave so the board never hits you or others. **Biomechanics** — Use a controlled pivot to change direction. Stay aware of incoming foam. Reorient the body and board while maintaining the safe relationship between surfer, board, and wave. **Common errors** — Body ends up between wave and board (dangerous); letting the board go loose; slow recovery — not ready to paddle after turn; forgetting the pre-turn shoulder check. **Mastery criteria** (MASTER-WB-06) — 1. 5 turns with the board controlled. 2. Body always between board and shore. 3. You finish each turn ready to paddle, not scrambling. **lessons STP-008** — Body always between the board and the wave.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (3):

  • Common errors (MASTER-WB-06): "Body ends up between wave and board (dangerous)" — está invertido, eso es lo correcto; debe decir "Board ends up between you and the wave (dangerous)".
  • Mastery 2 (MASTER-WB-06): "Body always between board and shore" → "Body always between the board and the wave — ocean side" (como ya dice lessons STP-008).
  • Mastery 1 (MASTER-WB-06 y lessons STP-008): "5 turns with the board controlled" — conteo.
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Shoulder check first — you turn in the gap between foams.
  2. You step around with the board through the 180° so you stay on its ocean side the whole turn — between the board and the wave, never the other way.
  3. Hands on the board the whole turn — it never floats loose.
  4. You end settled — nose pointing at the beach, hands on the rails — not scrambling.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Waist-deep, in the gap between foams: check over your shoulder, pivot the board 180° with your hands on it, stepping around so you stay on its ocean side the whole turn, and finish settled — nose to the beach, hands on the rails — ready to paddle.
drill:
Drill

Sin cambios (arena + agua calma + espuma más chica); sacar conteos y el '5 turns' del criterio 1.
juego:
Juego

Bodyguard

You're the board's bodyguard — the wave has to get through you first.

Rule: The wave reaches the board before it reaches you: you lost.

Measure: streak of turns without the wave getting past you

**Concept** — Return from waist-deep water to the sand safely — facing the waves, monitoring incoming foam, and adjusting your position if foam approaches. **Biomechanics** — Walk back under control while repeatedly checking behind for incoming foam. Maintain stable board handling and adjust direction if needed before continuing the return. **Common errors** — Turning your back fully to the waves; walking too fast; ignoring approaching foam; falling on slippery rocks. **Mastery criteria** — 1. After the session, walk in from waist depth reading the foam: look back before the first step and every few steps after, never with your back fully turned. Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Board floats level: not nose-up or nose-down.
  2. By the last mounts, one adjustment or none.

**Biomechanics** — Stay in the sweet spot first. Look over the shoulder to read the foam. Align the nose with the direction of the whitewater. Reset eyes forward and hold a long, ready body position before paddling. **Common errors** — Paddling without checking alignment; no shoulder check; aligned but pointing wrong direction; trying to align mid-paddle. **Mastery criteria** — 1. title: STP-012 · Paddle to Catch White Water
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-012-A · drill · Whitewater Catch Paddle Drill
  • MIS-WB-012 · mission · Catch Five Foam Waves By Paddling → Catch Foam Waves by Paddling (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Every first stroke full — no half-strokes.
  2. Elbow high on recovery, hand exits at the hip, head still.
  3. In calm water the board goes forward, not down.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 5 foam waves caught — no late starts.
  2. You keep paddling until the board accelerates with the wave — no early stops.
  3. Body long and pushing forward, not down.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-012 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria); identical text in lessons STP-012)

**Biomechanics** — Hands relaxed with fingers slightly together (not squeezed, not cupped). One arm then the other in a 1–2 rhythm. Fingertips enter cleanly, elbow stays high on recovery, and the pull drives water backward to move the board forward. Body stays long and stable like an arrow, with minimal head movement. **Common errors** — Late start; stopping before the board accelerates; pushing down instead of forward; choppy short strokes. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You start early on every attempt. 2. You don't stop until the board accelerates with the wave. 3. You catch 5 of 10 foam waves cleanly.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (3):

  • 'You catch 5 of 10 foam waves cleanly.' — count. Should read: 'You keep stroking until the board accelerates with the foam.'
  • Concept says 'Paddle aggressively' while the coach cue says 'Long strokes, not fast strokes.' — 'aggressively' reads as fast and choppy. Should read: 'Paddle with full commitment — start early, long strokes.'
  • Biomechanics only says 'start early' — no distance, and DISTANCE is the first key word. Add to Biomechanics: 'Start when the foam is still 1-4 m behind you.' (source: MIS-WB-011-A, coach catalogue: 'Commit to the paddle when whitewater is 1-4 m away').
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. First stroke goes in while the foam is still 1-4 m behind you — not when it hits the tail.
  2. Every stroke full and long in a one-two rhythm, elbow high on the recovery — no half-strokes, no short chop.
  3. The pull sends water back, not down — the board goes forward without dipping.
  4. Strokes keep their length and keep going until the board accelerates — no fading, no stopping early.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Prone in your sweet spot, nose pointing where the foam is going. When the foam is still 1-4 m behind you, start: first stroke full, then long one-two strokes that send water back, body long and head still. Keep stroking until you feel the board accelerate with the foam.

title: STP-013 · Cobra + Turn Left and Right
hoy:
HOY

  • MIS-WB-013 · mission · Direct Board Left and Right From Cobra
  • MIS-WB-013-A · mission · Prone Directional Ride (coach)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. On sand the order holds: hands, chest, eyes, rail.
  2. In calm water the board answers every time, on the called side.
  3. 3 lefts, 3 rights, each called first.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. The board turns the way you called it, every time.
  2. No accidental drift — the wave doesn't choose your line.
  3. 5 lefts + 5 rights, intentional.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-013 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria); identical text in lessons STP-013)

**Biomechanics** — Hands at rib height. Arms extend to lift the chest. Eyes look forward, then toward the intended direction. Pressure through the rail and engagement of the obliques begin the directional change. Slightly farther-back body position increases maneuverability; too far forward reduces turning ability. **Common errors** — Trying to direct without raising chest; not using eyes to lead; pressing the wrong rail; hands too far forward. **Mastery criteria** — 1. Board responds to direction every time. 2. Direction matches your stated intention. 3. You execute 5 left and 5 right turns intentionally.

  1. Hands on the rails at rib height — not out in front.
  2. Arms extend and the chest lifts before any turn.
  3. Eyes go first to the called side.
  4. Pressure on that rail, and the board turns where you look — not where the wave pushes.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Catch a foam wave and ride it in cobra: hands at your ribs, arms extended, chest up, eyes forward. Call the side before you turn, look that way, press that rail — and steer the board where you look. Switch sides across waves.

title: STP-014 · Prone Dismount
hoy:

  • MIS-WB-014 · mission · Exit 5 Rides via Prone Dismount → Exit the Ride With a Prone Dismount (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Hands never leave the rails until you are stable.
  2. You roll over one hip and land on your side or back — never face-first.
  3. The board stays with you on every rep.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 5 of 5 exits without losing the board — rails held until you're stable.
  2. You land in control, never face-first, no panic.
  3. You decided the moment — a chosen exit, not a panic exit.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-014 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria); identical text in lessons STP-014)

**Biomechanics** — Grab the rails at chest height. Shift back approximately 30 cm. Rotate over one hip with legs extended, then bring both knees to the chest. Point the soles of the feet in the same direction as the nose of the board and land while maintaining board control. **Common errors** — Diving off head-first; losing the board; letting go too early; panicking when the ride ends. **Mastery criteria** — 1. You exit 5 rides without losing the board. 2. You never let go of the rails until stable in the water. 3. You land controlled, never face-first.

La lección tiene un problema (2):

  • 'You exit 5 rides without losing the board.' — count. Should read: 'You exit with the rails in hand — the board never gets away.'
  • Biomechanics ends at 'land while maintaining board control' with no side named — 'come up on the ocean side' lives only in the drill. Add to the end of Biomechanics in STP-014 (MASTER-WB-06 and lesson STP-014): 'Land while maintaining board control: come up on the ocean side, board beside you on the beach side, rails still in hand — never between you and the next wave.'

Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Exit starts on your own call — say 'now' and go; in the water, while the board still glides, never when the wave throws you.
  2. Hands at chest height on the rails — and they stay there until you're stable in the water.
  3. Shift back, then roll over one hip — legs extended, knees to the chest, never head-first.
  4. Land on your side or back, on the ocean side of the board — never face-first.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

At the end of a foam ride, while the board still glides, decide the exit yourself. Grab the rails at chest height, shift back, roll over one hip with legs extended, then knees to your chest. Soles where the nose points, land on your side or back, and come up on the ocean side with the rails in hand.

title: STP-017 · Feet Position Center #2

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Back foot in FP2 — centered, back third — 5 of 5 in a row.
  2. Feet off the rails, weight on the front foot — the back foot is placed, not loaded.
  3. You look down and it is already there.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 5 of 5 pop-ups: back foot lands centered, in the back third, on neither rail.
  2. Board runs straight off the landing — no drift, no body compensation.
Lección (lessons STP-017 (fila propia: Biomechanics + Success Indicators + Common Errors + How you know you have it); MASTER-WB-06 § STP-017 dice lo mismo)

The board is designed to go forward and turn when the rails are pressed. If the feet do not land in the center, one rail is already being pressed and the board starts going in a direction without intention. That forces the body to compensate, creating disorder in posture. Position 2 is the neutral area where the back foot normally lands after the pop-up, giving a balance of stability and speed. | SI1: The feet land centered on the board and not close to the rails. SI2: The back foot lands in position number 2 with more consistency. SI3: The surfer connects with the board without obvious body compensation or posture disorder. | Common Errors: Foot landing in the wrong place; landing close to a rail; body compensation; posture disorder; landing too far forward or too far back; disconnection from the board. | How you know you have it — Back foot in FP2 on 5 of 5 pop-ups.

La lección tiene un problema (2):

  • Conteo en la lección (STP-017 y master): «Back foot in FP2 on 5 of 5 pop-ups.» → «Back foot lands in FP2 — centered on the stringer, back third — on the pop-up.»
  • La lección ubica FP2 solo como «neutral area where the back foot normally lands» (sin «back third», el criterio 2 queda sin fuente) y no dice que el pie de atrás se apoya SIN peso (doctrina 2-sep). mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Back foot lands between the rails — on neither one.
  2. Back foot lands in FP2 — the back third of the board.
  3. No shuffle after landing — the feet stay where they fell.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Foam rides. Pop up with one job: back foot to Position #2 — the back third, centered between the rails, no weight on it. A quick glance down, then ride. Off? Next wave, same job. [Card: MIS-WB-017 → title 'Land Your Back Foot in Position #2'; reps_recommended and time_estimate → empty.]

title: STP-018 · Power Stance / Posture
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-018-A · drill · Power Posture Drill
  • MIS-WB-018 · mission · Hold the Power Posture for 5 Seconds on 3 Rides → Hold the Power Posture on the Ride (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Shoulder arrows point where the board points, every rep.
  2. Weight FRONT foot, back knee toward the nose, toes across.
  3. Comfortable and active: no stiffening, no looking down.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 3 different rides, posture held ≥5 seconds without buckling: low, weight FRONT, back knee to the nose, shoulders where the board points.
  2. Active, not tense — hands and core on, eyes forward.

The upper body connects to the board by aiming the shoulders in the same direction as the nose of the board. Most of the weight stays on the front foot, while the back knee points forward. The front foot sits centered over the stringer, toes across the board rather than pointing at the nose, so toes and heel can push the rails. The back foot carries no weight: from the hip, the back knee points toward the nose. Flexion lowers the center of gravity and increases stability. The hands stay active and controlled, with scapular engagement, to support balance and direction. | Common Errors: Inactive scapula; shoulder collapsing forward; too much weight on the back foot; looking down; back knee not pointing forward; loose uncontrolled hands; no exhale; posture without activation. | How you know you have it — You hold the stance ≥5 seconds on 3 different rides.

La lección tiene un problema (4):

  • Conteo en la lección (STP-018 y master): «You hold the stance ≥5 seconds on 3 different rides.» → «You hold the stance for the whole ride.»
  • «Most of the weight stays on the front foot» (Biomechanics) y SI2 «most of the weight on the front foot» vs doctrina: pie de atrás SIN peso → «All the weight on the front foot; the back foot carries none.» (la misma lección ya lo dice dos frases después).

Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Both shoulders aim where the nose points — eyes forward.
  2. Front foot centered on the stringer, toes across the board — not at the nose — all your weight on it: hips over the front foot, the tail never sinks.
  3. From the hip, the back knee points toward the nose.
  4. Low: knees bent, hands up and active — no stiffening, no lock-out.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Foam rides. Pop up, land, and lock the Power Posture: chest to the nose, shoulders aimed where the board goes, front foot centered on the stringer with toes across the board, all your weight on it, back knee pointing at the nose, low. Exhale and keep it alive for the whole ride — if it slips, fix it as you go. [Card: MIS-WB-018 → title 'Hold the Power Posture Through the Ride'; reps_recommended and time_estimate → empty.]

title: STP-019 · Impulse — Forward Momentum
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-019-A · drill · Impulse Forward Speed Drill
  • MIS-WB-019-A · mission · Full Sequence + Impulse
  • MIS-WB-019 · mission · Generate Speed via Impulse on 3 Rides → Generate Speed With Impulse (título sin conteo)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Every rep starts and ends in Power Posture.
  2. Flex, touch, push, extend flow as one movement — no half-touch.
  3. By the last reps you run it without thinking.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. Every time the board slows, the full impulse shows — flex, touch, push, extend — on at least 3 rides.
  2. After it, the board speeds up and the ride runs longer.
Lección (lessons STP-019 (fila propia: Biomechanics + Success Indicators + Common Errors + How you know you have it); MASTER-WB-06 § STP-019 para los Common errors cortos)

The surfer flexes forward by bringing the chest toward the knees and bending the legs, then touches the water and pushes forward with one or two hands. At the same time, the body and legs extend, releasing stored energy and projecting it forward. This helps the board regain speed and stability. | SI1: Uses the hands against the water with clear intention to generate forward momentum. SI2: Combines flexion and extension instead of only touching the water with no real push. SI3: Recovers speed and stability when getting stuck, slowing down, or losing balance. | Common Errors: No leg flexion; chest not moving forward; half movement with no real push; not extending after the touch; not using the tool when speed is needed. (MASTER: Not extending fully; wrong timing; touching water too soon; no upward extension.) | How you know you have it — You execute impulse on 3 different rides.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (2):

  • Conteo en la lección (STP-019 y master): «You execute impulse on 3 different rides.» → «You fire the impulse every time the board slows.»
  • MASTER-WB-06 § STP-019 Common errors: «no upward extension» contradice Biomechanics («projecting it forward») y la cadena push · extend → «no forward extension».
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Flex: knees bend, chest drops toward them.
  2. Touch: one or both hands reach down and touch the water.
  3. Push: the hands push against the water — a real push, not a half-touch.
  4. Extend forward: body and legs spring ahead — forward, not up.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Foam rides in Power Posture. The moment the board loses speed, that's your trigger: flex — knees bend, chest to the knees — touch the water with one or both hands, push and extend forward. Feel the board pick up again and settle back into posture, ready for the next one. [Cards: MIS-WB-019 → title 'Impulse When the Board Slows'; reps_recommended and time_estimate → empty. MIS-WB-019-A (chain) → reps_recommended and time_estimate → empty; its 3 criteria are already count-free and stay.]

The flat water is lava; the board is the only cool spot as long as it keeps moving.

title: STP-020 · Starfish Dismount

  • MIS-WB-020-A · mission · Starfish on Every Ride (coach)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Bend first, then open — arms and legs wide before falling.
  2. Straight back, face up — never sideways, never head-first, no jump.
  3. Wide and calm, not stiff.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 3 starfish exits: no injury, no lost board, no headfirst dive.
  2. You decide before losing balance; you fall backward, wide and calm — not stiff.
  3. You land in the foam every time.
Lección (lessons STP-020 (fila propia: Biomechanics + Success Indicators + Common Errors + How you know you have it); MASTER-WB-06 § STP-020 dice lo mismo)

The surfer slightly bends the knees, opens the body wide with arms and legs, and falls back onto the foam. The wider body position creates resistance and helps reduce forward penetration toward the bottom, while the foam gives more cushioning than falling ahead into shallower water. | SI1: Chooses to dismount before getting too close to the shore or impact area. SI2: Opens the body into a star shape with arms and legs wide. SI3: Falls onto the foam in a controlled way, reducing impact and avoiding unsafe exits. | Common Errors: Falling to the side instead of back; not opening the arms; not opening the legs; not bending first; doing it too late; jumping; forgetting to dismount; landing outside the foam. | How you know you have it — 3 starfish exits without injury or losing board. Body wide and calm during fall — not stiff. You decide BEFORE losing balance.

La lección tiene un problema (1):

  1. You go while you're still steady and still in the foam — before the shallows, before any wobble.
  2. Knees bend first, then arms and legs open wide into a star.
  3. You fall straight back, face up — no jump, no sideways, never head-first.
  4. Loose all the way down — not stiff.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Every standing ride ends on purpose. While you're still balanced and still in the foam — before the shallows — bend your knees, open arms and legs into a star and fall straight back onto the foam, face up. No jump, no dive. [Card: MIS-WB-020 → title 'End Every Ride with a Starfish'; reps_recommended and time_estimate → empty.]

Drill

title: STP-021 · Turn Backside

HOY

  • MIS-WB-021 · mission · Execute 3 Backside Turns → Turn Backside on the Wave (título sin conteo)
  • MIS-WB-021-A · mission · Backside Turn in Water (coach)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Eyes and neck lead, shoulders stay forward.
  2. Chain in order — look, oblique, hip, heel — rail down, stance held.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 3 turns where the board changed direction because of the rail — not drift.
  2. Each step in order, posture held, no shoulder spin.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-021 (Biomechanics + Common errors + Mastery criteria) + lessons STP-021 (How your body does it + Success Indicators + How you know you have it) + sequences SEQ-4.0-018 (expectation_standard: "initiates small backside direction change"))

Biomechanics — The movement begins with the eyes and neck turning toward the intended direction. The shoulders remain pointing forward. The oblique activates, the hip follows, and the energy travels down to the foot, ending in heel pressure to sink the rail. The front-foot pressure remains important for stability while the board crosses. / Common errors — Skipping the look (no visual lead); body twists without eye lead; rail engagement without rotation; falling weight back. (…rotating the shoulders instead of keeping them forward; back foot too far forward; losing energy before the rail change.) / Mastery criteria — 1. 3 turns where board responded to rail input — looking clearly toward the intended backside direction first. 2. Sequence executed in order: look → oblique → hip → heel → rail, without losing posture. 3. Board changes direction, not just drifts.

La lección tiene un problema (3):

  • CONTEO en Mastery criteria 1 (MASTER-WB-06) y bullet 1 de 'How you know you have it' (STP-021): "3 turns where board responded to rail input" → "You look clearly toward the backside direction before the turn — and the board responds to the rail." (solo se quita el '3 turns'; el criterio 1 es LOOK FIRST, el drift ya es el criterio 3).
  • COLETILLA en el pie plantilla de las 25 lecciones (fuera del cambio de esta secuencia): "Your coach confirms mastery in the water." — si se toca globalmente, quitar solo eso y conservar "consistently across (3) different sessions" (regla de consistencia del Canon, mastery ≠ un día bueno; el 3 lo decide Marcelo).

mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Head turns backside first — eyes and neck only, shoulders stay with the nose.
  2. The turn comes from the middle — oblique twists, hip follows — not from the arms or shoulders.
  3. The heel presses the heel-side rail down while the front foot keeps its weight — nothing sits back on the tail.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

On a ride with room to turn, look backside first — eyes and neck only, shoulders stay with the nose. Twist the oblique, drive the hip, and press the heel-side rail down while the front foot keeps its weight. A small change of direction is enough — but it has to come from the rail, not drift.

  • MIS-WB-022-A · mission · Frontside Turn in Water (coach)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. Eyes lead frontside before the body — shoulders stay with the nose.
  2. Chest forward, weight on the front foot, no buckling, stance preserved.
  3. Skateboard crosses frontside without looking forced; backside just as clean.

  1. 3 turns where the board changed direction from the rail — not drift.
  2. Posture connected, no buckling forward.

Biomechanics — The surfer starts from posture, keeps the shoulders pointing in the same direction as the nose of the board, turns the neck to look toward the frontside direction, activates the oblique, and maintains pressure on the front foot. The movement works when the body stays connected and the rail change happens with control. / Common errors — Buckling forward (collapsing posture); losing the rail mid-turn; eyes following body instead of leading; weight shifts back. (…inactive scapula; both arms reaching forward; disconnected body; poor foot placement.) / Success Indicators — 1. Looks clearly toward the intended frontside direction before and during the turn. 2. Uses the oblique and maintains posture instead of disconnecting the body. 3. La lección tiene un problema (5):

  • CONTEO en Mastery criteria 1 (MASTER-WB-06) y bullet 1 de 'How you know you have it' (STP-022): "3 frontside turns where board responded" → "You look toward the frontside direction before and during the turn — and the board responds to the rail." (solo se quita el número; se conserva el 'before and during', que es el Success Indicator 1 y el Common error 'eyes following body').
  • CRITERIO CRUZADO en Mastery criteria 3 / bullet 3 de 'How you know you have it': "You can do both backside (STP-021) and frontside cleanly, crossing toward frontside without looking forced or unstable" — repite STP-021 y 'without looking forced or unstable' es juicio, no observable → "The board crosses frontside on the rail — no wobble, no sitting back."

  • REFERENCIA ROTA + 'TSS' en MASTER-WB-06 § STP-022: "Drill reference — TSS-022 — Frontside Rail Change Drill" → "Drill reference — DRL-WB-022-A — Frontside Rail Change Drill".

Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Head turns frontside first and stays turned through the whole turn — it leads, shoulders stay with the nose.
  2. The oblique turns the torso — the arms don't swing the turn, never both reaching forward.
  3. Chest stays low and to the nose without folding at the hips — no buckling.
  4. Toes press the front-side rail down with the weight still on the front foot — the rail holds through the whole turn, it doesn't let go halfway.

On a ride with room to turn, pick your line frontside and keep your head turned to it for the whole turn — shoulders stay with the nose. Fire the oblique, keep the chest low and to the nose — no folding at the hips — and press the front-side rail down with your toes, weight on the front foot. Drill

mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Fingertips slice in first, hands relaxed — no slap, no splash.
  2. One arm at a time, elbow passing over your ear on every stroke.
  3. Each stroke drives you forward, not up — a long pull, the nose doesn't bob — the same stroke whether you cruise, hold steady or sprint.
  4. Body straight like an arrow, head still — no side-to-side swing.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Paddle from the shore to the lineup on your own. Settle into the sweet spot, then one arm at a time: elbow over the ear, fingertips in first, long stroke pushing forward — body like an arrow, head still. Shift gears on purpose — cruise, steady, sprint — you decide when, and arrive with energy left.

Rule: One slap on the water wakes it up — round over. Every paddle out is a new round.

title: STP-024 · Turtle Roll
seq: White #5 — Independence (STP-023 Paddle Out · STP-024 Turtle Roll · STP-025 Turn Left and Right Lying on Board)
hoy:
HOY

  • DRL-WB-024-A · drill · Turtle Roll Safety Drill
  • MIS-WB-024 · mission · Pass Through 5 Foam Waves via Turtle Roll → Pass Foam Waves With the Turtle Roll (título sin conteo)
  • MIS-WB-024-A · mission · Align → Roll → Control → Turn → Catch (coach)

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. 5 rolls, hands never leave the rails.
  2. Elbows on the board, every roll.
  3. Each roll ends chest to center, paddling right away.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 5 rolls, board never lost.
  2. Each roll starts about 1 meter before the foam.
  3. You come up paddling every time — no panic.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-024 — Turtle Roll (Biomechanics Set up/Roll/Recover + Common errors + Mastery criteria); espejo idéntico en lessons STP-024 (How your body does it + How you know you have it))

**Biomechanics** 1. Set up — Align the nose of the board with the direction the foam is coming from. Grab both rails firmly with your hands. Keep your elbows on top of the board to protect your face from the bottom […]. 2. Roll — Tilt the board sideways to begin going under, then continue until the board is upside down with you hanging below. Your body stays close to the board. Hold through the turbulence — do not let go. 3. Recover — Scissor kick with your legs while using one arm to leverage the board back to flat. Return your chest to the center of the board. Resume paddling immediately. **Common errors** — Poor alignment; wrong timing; releasing the board mid-roll; no elbow protection; bad recovery (no return to center). **Mastery criteria** 1. 5 rolls without losing the board. 2. Timing is correct — about 1 meter before foam. 3. You recover to paddling each time.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (3):

  • Mastery criteria 1: "5 rolls without losing the board." — CONTEO; debería decir "The board never leaves your hands — through the whole roll and the recovery."
  • Biomechanics 1: "Align the nose of the board with the direction the foam is coming from" — no contradice la doctrina (el Concept ya dice "Align the nose against the foam direction"); unificar a la frase canónica en el master y en el espejo STP-024: "Point the nose into the incoming foam — against the direction the wave's energy travels."
  • Mastery criteria 2: "Timing is correct — about 1 meter before foam." — no es conteo de reps, pero es una medida; como ejecución: "You go under just before the foam hits — about a meter out — never after it has reached you."
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. Nose pointing straight into the incoming foam — square to it, not sideways.
  2. Hands locked on both rails, elbows on top of the deck — all the way through the roll.
  3. Upside down, body tight to the board through the turbulence — the board never leaves your hands.
  4. Board back flat and you're on it — chest in the center, paddling again immediately.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Paddle out through real whitewater. As each wall of foam comes, point the nose straight into it, lock both rails with your elbows on the deck, and roll under just before it hits. Hang tight beneath the board through the turbulence, then scissor kick, lever it flat, chest back to center and paddle on.
drill:
Drill

Sin cambios de estaciones (arena → piscina/agua calma → espuma más chica, que es la simulación válida para manejo de tabla). ALIGN solo se observa en la estación de espuma; RAILS · ELBOWS · HOLD · RECOVER se ven en piscina/agua calma. Corregir la frase de alineación al texto de doctrina y sacar los conteos (3 · 3 · 5 reps) del Simulate y de success_criteria.
juego:
Juego

The Shell

You're a turtle and the board is your shell — the foam is just weather passing over it.

Rule: If you come up without your shell (the board leaves your hands), you're a naked turtle: round over.

Measure: Streak of foam walls passed inside your shell.
nota: RECOVER: las dos objeciones coincidían en agregar "paddling right away"; elegí la versión de un solo observable (tabla plana · pecho al centro · remando ya) y el mecanismo kick + lever queda en la instrucción, porque bajo la espuma no se ve y el criterio debe servir igual para drill y misión. La coletilla "protect your face from the bottom" de la lección se refiere al fondo (hull) de la tabla, no al fondo del mar; conviene reescribirla ("so the board can't hit your face"). title: STP-025 · Turn Left and Right Lying on Board

Criterios del drill hoy:

  1. 5 turns per mode in calm water, both sides, each mode distinct — the board goes where you meant.
  2. Every turn ends ready to paddle, never stuck out of position.

Criterios de la misión hoy:

  1. 6 turns: 3 left, 3 right, each on purpose and controlled.
  2. You chose the mode for the situation.
  3. Every turn ends ready to paddle — never out of position.
Lección (lessons MASTER-WB-06 § STP-025 — Turn Left and Right Lying on Board (Biomechanics — three canonical modes + Common errors + Mastery criteria); espejo idéntico en lessons STP-025 (How your body does it + How you know you have it))

**Biomechanics — three canonical modes** A · One-side paddling — Paddle with only one arm to redirect the board. The asymmetric force rotates the nose toward the opposite side. B · Circular hand motion — Place both hands in the water and move them in opposite circular directions […] spins the board around its center. C · Seated pivot — Sit up on the board with your hips moved back toward the tail. This shifts the buoyancy point and lets the board pivot more easily. Use your hands and feet to assist the rotation. **Common errors** — Trying to turn from too far forward; weak directional paddling; poor seated pivot; not moving back enough; turning but not staying ready to paddle. **Mastery criteria** 1. You execute 6 direction changes (3 each side) in a session. 2. Each one is intentional, controlled, ready-to-paddle. 3. You choose the right mode for the situation.
warn:
La lección tiene un problema (1):

  • Mastery criteria 1: "You execute 6 direction changes (3 each side) in a session." — CONTEO; debería decir "You turn the board to either side on purpose — the nose ends where you meant and you're ready to paddle."
mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. The nose swings to the side you called — left or right on purpose, not wherever the water takes it.
  2. Strokes on one side only, long pulls — the nose swings away from the paddling arm.
  3. Pivot on the spot — the board spins on its center, nose swinging while the board stays put: hands circling opposite ways lying down, or seated with hips back toward the tail, hands and feet sweeping.
  4. Every turn ends with you flat in the sweet spot, hands ready for the first stroke — no re-adjusting.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

In the lineup or the paddle zone, pick where the nose should point before you move, then turn it there — to either side. Use the mode the moment asks for: one-arm strokes to swing it while you're moving; hands circling opposite ways, or sitting back on the tail with hands and feet, to spin on the spot. Each turn ends with you flat and ready for the first stroke.
drill:
Drill

Sin cambios de estaciones (arena en seco → agua calma a la cintura, sin olas). En arena solo se simula la forma de ONE · PIVOT (círculos acostado y sentado con caderas atrás); TURN/READY (la nariz termina donde elegiste y ya estás en posición de remo) solo se observa en agua calma. Sacar "3 reps per mode / 5 reps per mode" del Simulate y de success_criteria.
juego:
Juego

Lock On

Your nose is a laser pointer: call a target — a tree on the beach, a headland, a buoy — and swing the beam onto it.

Rule: The beam has to stop dead on the target. Short of it or past it, the laser missed: new target, new round.

Measure: Streak of targets locked without a miss.

READY sigue distinto del RECOVER de STP-024 (acá terminás listo tras el giro; allá salís remando tras el roll).

Not paddling harder — paddling with purpose. | V1 — Cruising 30–40% · Active recovery · maintain position | V2 — Working 50–60% · Sustained displacement | V3 — Catching 70–80% · Reach peak with time to adjust | V4 — Sprint 90–100% · Take-off · critical saves | Cue: "Match the speed to the wave, not the panic." — COACH-STP-027 / How you correct it: Always V4 (panic) → "You're burning the tank." · Short stroke → "Push past your hip — that's the power." · Doesn't breathe in sprint → "V3/V4 = 1:1 breathing." · Speed vs cadence → "It's reach + power, not cadence."

  • Conteo en la misión de la lección: "Choose the correct speed without external instruction in 3 of every 4 paddle-ins, across 2 consecutive sessions." → debería ser la instrucción de ejecución (nombrar la velocidad y cambiar en la palabra; dónde se usa cada una); reps y sesiones van al plan del alumno.

mision:
Criterios de ejecución — mismos para drill y misión

  1. The switch is sharp — one stroke at the old speed, the next at the new one, no drifting in between.
  2. Each speed looks clearly different from the one before it — nothing is paddled at V4 by default.
  3. The stroke keeps its full reach past the hip at every speed — more speed is more push, never a shorter stroke.
  4. Breathing stays in rhythm with the stroke at V3 and V4 — no held breath in the sprint.

Misión — la instrucción en el agua

Call Your Speed (MIS-YB-027)

In the lineup, drive your paddling like gears: say the speed out loud and switch on the word — 'one… now three… four… two'. Use each change where it is needed: two or three to get out of the impact zone, four to get clear of a wave about to land on you, three into the peak and four for the take-off, back to one to hold your spot.

Cue. “Match the speed to the wave, not the panic.”

You get one gear. Pick it before your first stroke, and the gearbox welds shut until you turn to go.

  1. The elbow is THROWN — with power, not lifted.
  2. The elbow goes UP — never down.
  3. The other arm stays alive: the two arms draw an M.
  4. The back foot follows the elbow — it pivots and the tail swings.

On backside waves, run the whole chain — bottom turn, Choke, Tapaloco — and close it with the Elbow: throw the elbow of the Tapaloco arm up with power, the other arm alive so both draw an M, scapulas pulling together, back foot pivoting after the elbow so the tail swings. title: STP-047 · Hold

Lección (lessons.STP-047 (description_md) + COACH-BB-SEQ12 (coach lesson of the sequence))

The body during the Hold position: Maintains the Cruz position (same as STP-041 + STP-046) · Stays FLEXED in the Cruz · your leg stays bent · Does NOT extend the leg until the Grenade is about to be thrown · Your weight stays on your FRONT leg · All the details of the Cruz (palms forward · chest open · eyes over shoulder · oblique · rail change) are PRESERVED during the Hold. When the Grenade fires → leg extends fully → return to posture. Common mistakes: Cutback in two movements (you broke the Hold) · Releasing the Hold too early · Extending the leg before the Grenade · Losing weight forward during Hold · Losing the Cruz details during Hold. How you know you have it: I held the Cruz for the full arc (no break) · My leg stayed flexed throughout the Hold · My weight stayed forward · All my Cruz details (palms, chest, eyes, oblique) stayed engaged during the Hold

  2. Legs stay flexed for the whole Hold — they extend only with the Grenade.
